safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(لإيلاف) is attached to the coming (يعبدوا) [Note: i.e. for the sake of the Quraysh's habituation.. let the Qurayshis worship the Lord of this House – this is the view of al-Khalīl and, after him, al-Zamakhsharī – while al-Ṭabarī takes the lām as one of wonder, so that it is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "wonder at the Quraysh's habituation and their abandoning the worship of the Lord of the House".. It is also possible for the prepositional phrase to be attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "He did that", i.e. the destruction of the Companions of the Elephant.], (إيلافهم) is a badal of the first, genitive; (رحلة) is a direct object of the maṣdar إيلافهم; (the fāʾ) is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis of an implied condition; (اللام) is the lām of command; (الذي) is a relative in the position of accusative, a naʿt of ربّ; (من جوع) is attached to (أطعمهم), and (من) is causal [Note: or, by taking أطعمهم to include the meaning of "satisfied them", (من) is for the beginning of the range.]; (من خوف) is attached to (آمنهم)..
Clause: «يعبدوا ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: if they do not worship Him for any other favour, let them worship Him for their habituation, for it is the most evident favour.
And the clause: «أطعمهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause: «آمنهم» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.

* Morphology:
(1) إيلاف: the regular maṣdar of the quadriliteral آلف, whose original is أألف on the wazn أفعل, or the maṣdar of أولف on the wazn أفعل. On the first view the hamza was lightened and turned into yāʾ because of the kasra before it; on the second view an i'lāl by substitution occurred, the original being أولاف: the letter before the wāw took a kasra, so it turned into yāʾ.. The wazn of إيلاف is إفعال.
(قريش): a proper name of the famous Arab tribe; it was said to be a diminutive of endearment (tarkhīm) from قويرش, the diminutive of قارش; its plural is قرش with two ḍammas.
(2) رحلة: it was said to be a generic noun, hence it is in the singular; or an ism maṣdar meaning الارتحال (travelling), put in the singular as there is no risk of confusion; its wazn is فعلة with kasra then sukūn.
(الشتا): the name of the well-known season, derived from شتا يشتو (class of نصر); in it the wāw was changed to hamza because it comes at the end after a quiescent alif, its original being شتاو; its wazn is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ.
(الصيف): the name of the well-known season, derived from صاف يصيف (class of ضرب); its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Benefits:
- The winter and summer journey:
Ibn ʿAbbās said: They used to winter in Mecca and summer in al-Ṭāʾif, so Allah the Exalted commanded them to remain in the Sanctuary and to worship the Lord of this House. Most said: They had two journeys every year for trade: a journey in winter to Yemen because it is warmer, and a journey in summer to Syria. The Sanctuary was a barren valley with no crops and no livestock; the Quraysh lived by their trade and their journeys, and no one would harm them. They used to say: the Quraysh are the people of Allah's sanctuary and the custodians of His House; and the Arabs acknowledged and honoured them. Therefore, were it not for the two journeys they would have had no standing in Mecca, and were it not for the security beside the House they would not have been able to move about.
